chunks: Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn al-Kharidj, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, exempted your Prophet from facing from his community what the prophets faced from their communities, and He made that for us.

key_terms.عَلَيْنَا: Upon us (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What specific trial was Prophet Muhammad exempted from that other prophets faced?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates a unique divine mercy where Prophet Muhammad (saw) was spared the intense rejection and tribulation faced by earlier prophets, shifting that burden of trial onto the Ahl al-Bayt. This highlights the theological concept of the Imams as the enduring custodians of the message, bearing the weight of communal deviation and preserving the faith through their own trials. The hadith underscores the continuity of prophetic struggle, now transferred to the progeny of the Prophet to ensure the preservation of divine guidance.

en.sarwar: 353. Yahya Al-Halby, from Haroun Bin Al-Kharjat, from Abu Baseer, who has said: Abu Abdullah (a.s.)
